description: HAWK-I is the VLT High-Acuity Wide-field K-band Imager. Kissler-Patig et al. 2008 describe it as a 0.9–2.4 μm camera with four 2k×2k arrays over a 7.5×7.5 arcmin field. These bands are ESO's filter-transmission scans.
facility_description: The ESO Very Large Telescope stands at the Paranal Observatory in Chile.

notes: The public filters.html page and the filters/ directory URL now redirect to an ESO login. The individual .dat files are still public, and their headers give the scan temperature. Both hawki_Knew.dat and hawki_Kold.dat are labeled simply 'K filter curve'. Kissler-Patig et al. 2008, A&A 491, 941 is the instrument paper; the usual bibcode 2008A&A...491..941K did not resolve in check_refs, so the DOI is used. Pirard et al. 2004 is the design paper. No magnitude system is stated in the file headers. The current ESO directory listing used here has no NB0984 file; that scan is only in the HAWK-I/HAWK-I set. DetectorType photon, DetectorTypeSource inferred (2026-10-26): no owner states the integration convention for the curve file, but the ESO .dat files are filter curves only ('BrGamma filter curve @ T=90K', Wavelength (nm), T (%)), and HAWK-I's detectors are 'a mosaic of four Hawaii 2RG 2048 * 2048 pixels detectors' (https://www.eso.org/sci/facilities/paranal/instruments/hawki/overview.html), so the curves integrate as photon counters. The source is 'inferred' because this rests on the published curve content and the documented detector, not on an explicit owner statement.

BrGamma.Comments: Brackett-gamma filter. The ESO file header reads 'BrGamma filter curve @ T=90K'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.

CH4.Comments: Methane filter. The ESO file header reads 'CH4 filter curve @ T=90K'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.

H.Comments: H-band filter. The ESO file header reads 'H filter curve @ T=87K' and 'H 2 (S5-235-1)'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.
H.DetectorType_note: SVO's Paranal/HAWKI.H (captured 2025-09-06) is the same curve as NJM's within resampling (SVO/NJM ratio 0.996-1.004 where both exceed 5 % of peak); only the label differs. SVO gives energy with no stated basis; NJM's photon (inferred) rests on ESO's filter-only curve files and HAWK-I's Hawaii 2RG photon-counting detectors (see the instrument notes).

H2.Comments: H2 filter. The ESO file header reads 'H2 filter curve @ T=90K'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.

J.Comments: J-band filter. The ESO file header reads 'J filter curve @ T=87K' and 'J 2 (X1-3778-P1,S1-334-P1,SN012)'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.
J.DetectorType_note: SVO's Paranal/HAWKI.J (captured 2025-11-17) is close to NJM's curve, probably the same scan resampled (SVO/NJM ratio 1.000-1.010 where both exceed 5 % of peak); only the label differs. SVO gives energy with no stated basis; NJM's photon (inferred) rests on ESO's filter-only curve files and HAWK-I's Hawaii 2RG photon-counting detectors (see the instrument notes).

Knew.Comments: The file ESO names hawki_Knew.dat. Its header reads 'K filter curve @ T=90K' and does not use the word Knew. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent. ESO's hawki_Knew.dat and hawki_Kold.dat are byte-identical (SHA-256 6a7a8850...59a5a1, both headed '# K filter curve @ T=90K', fetched 2026-10-26), although ESO's filter table (https://www.eso.org/sci/facilities/paranal/instruments/hawki/inst.html) lists them as two filters: 'Ks (1)' = hawki_Kold.dat, '(1) Filter used from Aug 2007 until Dec 3, 2007. Showed some structure for the Nov 2007 Science Verification run.', and 'Ks (2)' = hawki_Knew.dat, '(2) New Ks filter, used starting Jan 2008.' NJM's Knew and Kold therefore carry the same curve (sample rows identical); ESO has not published a separate curve for the 2007 filter.

Kold.Comments: The file ESO names hawki_Kold.dat. Its header also reads 'K filter curve @ T=90K'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent. ESO's hawki_Knew.dat and hawki_Kold.dat are byte-identical (SHA-256 6a7a8850...59a5a1, both headed '# K filter curve @ T=90K', fetched 2026-10-26), although ESO's filter table (https://www.eso.org/sci/facilities/paranal/instruments/hawki/inst.html) lists them as two filters: 'Ks (1)' = hawki_Kold.dat, '(1) Filter used from Aug 2007 until Dec 3, 2007. Showed some structure for the Nov 2007 Science Verification run.', and 'Ks (2)' = hawki_Knew.dat, '(2) New Ks filter, used starting Jan 2008.' NJM's Knew and Kold therefore carry the same curve (sample rows identical); ESO has not published a separate curve for the 2007 filter.

NB1060.Comments: Narrow-band filter NB1060. The ESO file header reads 'NB1060 filter curve @ T=90K'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.
NB1060.DetectorType_note: SVO's Paranal/HAWKI.NB1060 (captured 2022-09-26) is close to NJM's curve, probably the same scan resampled (SVO/NJM ratio 0.970-1.055 where both exceed 5 % of peak); only the label differs. SVO gives energy with no stated basis; NJM's photon (inferred) rests on ESO's filter-only curve files and HAWK-I's Hawaii 2RG photon-counting detectors (see the instrument notes).

NB2090.Comments: Narrow-band filter NB2090. The ESO file header reads 'NB2090 filter curve @ T=90K'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.
NB2090.DetectorType_note: SVO's Paranal/HAWKI.NB2090 (captured 2022-10-06) is close to NJM's curve, probably the same scan resampled (SVO/NJM ratio 1.000-1.029 where both exceed 5 % of peak); only the label differs. SVO gives energy with no stated basis; NJM's photon (inferred) rests on ESO's filter-only curve files and HAWK-I's Hawaii 2RG photon-counting detectors (see the instrument notes).

Y.Comments: Y-band filter. The ESO file header reads 'Y filter curve @ T=87K' and 'Y 3 (Iz881,SN003)'. Wavelength column is nanometres and transmission is percent.
